title: Neural Codec Language Models are Zero-Shot Text to Speech Synthesizers
layout_note: Right: two wide decoder bands stacked, the NAR Transformer Decoder (blue) on top and the AR Transformer Decoder (green) below, each fed from below by a pale-green G2P box (Text) and a pale-blue EnCodec box (waveform glyph) plus code tokens; a bold title 'Conditional Codec Language Modeling' at the bottom. Left: two 4x4 attention-mask grids (NAR all white, AR with grey upper-right cells) and a two-swatch key.
grouping: The decoder stages are the two full-width colour bands (blue NAR, green AR); their inputs are small pale tinted rounded boxes under each band; the attention-mask panel is a separate left column with its own titles ('NAR: attend to all tokens', 'AR: c_i only attends to left').
shapes_depth: Flat wide rectangles with no outline for the decoders and large centred text; small pale rounded boxes for G2P and EnCodec; a blue vertical-bar waveform glyph under EnCodec; mask grids of outlined squares, white or grey-filled. Tokens are bold-italic math symbols on thin arrows; AR feedback drawn as dash-dot curved loops.
proposed_highlight: Each stage is one saturated full-width band with its name in large type (NAR blue, AR green), the only strong colours in the figure; the inputs below are drawn in paler versions of the same hues.
lesson: Beside a stack of decoder stages, draw each stage's attention mask as a small white/grey grid with the same token symbols on its axes, so causal vs full attention is shown rather than stated.
notes: venue = arXiv (no venue printed on the first page); year = arXiv preprint year. Fig. 1 is a simpler overview (prompt icons into one 'Neural Codec Language Modeling' band); Fig. 3 was chosen because it draws the AR/NAR structure and the attention masks.

arrangement.units: left: an unframed column of two attention-mask grids with a swatch key; right: two full-width coloured decoder bands stacked (NAR above AR), each with its own input boxes beneath, titled in bold at the bottom
arrangement.inputs_as: the word 'Text' into a G2P box and a blue waveform glyph into an EnCodec box, then rows of italic code-token symbols
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; output token symbols sit above each band
arrangement.shared: G2P and EnCodec are drawn again under each decoder band

taxonomy.note: training 'other' = a non-autoregressive stage that predicts the remaining codec quantizer levels in parallel

insights.structure: Two wide decoder bands are stacked on the right (NAR blue above AR green), each with G2P and EnCodec input boxes underneath, and a separate left column holds the matching attention-mask grids.
insights.data: Speech is a blue vertical-bar waveform glyph, text is the word 'Text', and every token is a typeset italic symbol (c_{0,1}, c~, <EOS>) on its own thin arrow instead of a drawn cell.
insights.emphasis: The two decoder bands are the only saturated fills and carry the largest type; the AR band's dash-dot loops from each output back to the next input make the autoregression the figure's most distinctive mark.
insights.flow: Inputs rise from the boxes into each band and outputs leave upward; in the AR band dash-dot curves loop every output down to the next input position, while the NAR band takes an NAR ID j on a dashed arrow at its right.
insights.avoid: The NAR stage sits above the AR stage although it runs second, so reading top-down gives the wrong order, and the mask grids have no connector to the bands they describe.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
